newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end lower, weak fundamentals hurt mood.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end lower, weak fundamentals hurt mood.

text.p: South Korean stocks ended Monday's trading lower, weighed down by weak fundamentals, brokers said.
The government's refusal to confirm speculation that real-name financial transaction rules would be eased for trading in long-term bonds also hurt the mood, they added.
The stock index ended 7.72 points lower at a provisional 667.35. Declining shares far outpaced advancers 611 to 205.
"The market's environment continues to be weak, leading to follow-through selling from Saturday's decline," said a Seoul Securities broker.
Interest rates continued to climb to record highs. Near the end of trading on Monday, the benchmark three-year corporate bonds were trading at 12.65 percent, a new year high.
Customer deposits at brokerage houses remain on a downtrend. On Saturday, brokers estimated deposits at 2.8 trillion won, down from a year high of 3.05 trillion in February.

Last week, shares climbed on hopes that the government would soon revise regulations on real-name financial transactions after new Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik told reporters that the current laws needed amending. But no action has been seen in that direction, dashing investor hopes.

Hopes are also dimming on an earlier-than-expected boost in the foreign shareholders' ceiling, currently set at 20 percent, brokers said. This limit is scheduled to be eased to 23 percent some time this year.
No impact was seen from news that amendments to a new version of a controversial labour law were due to be submitted to parliament on Monday after the market closed.
Dainong topped the most actives list, losing 460 won to 8,100. Midopa Department Store, the core company of the Dainong Group, is being targetted for a hostile takeover by Shindongbang.
Midopa lost 3,000 won to 35,200, and Shindongbang shed 2,700 won to 37,400.
Sammi Steel rebounded 200 won to 3,500. It had fallen recently on talk of financial difficulties.
Late afternoon bargain hunting erased some of POSCO's losses. It ended down 800 won to 41,200, after touching its limit low of 38,700.
The March futures contract fell 0.85 of a point to 67.40, while the KOSPI 200 index declined 0.99 of a point to 67.29.
